about: The bench's rendered pieces for IR Capture (desktop-bench, branch look; first made 2026-11-03 by helper irkit, rebuilt 2026-11-10 from the white-light renders). Sizes in px are the file's pixels; points (pt) are SwiftUI points, px_per_pt says how many of the 1x file's pixels make a point (the @2x file has twice). capInsets are SwiftUI EdgeInsets in points for Image(nsImage:).resizable(capInsets:resizingMode:) on an NSImage whose size is set in points (SwellKit.swift's SwellPictures does it). rects are in the named file's pixels, origin top left.

ref.frame_note: frame-* pieces: 1 pt = 1 ref px of the bench's 1440x900 layout; the 1x picture has 1.6 px a pt, the @2x 3.2
ref.rack_note: rack units and the capture player have no fixed point size: 10 pt a cm (the Tools views' scale) makes a 3U rack unit (1128 x 342 px at 22.5 px/cm) 501 x 152 pt; px_per_pt = pxcm / 10

rack-speaker.how: a whole rack unit: draw it scaled to fit (no slicing); each element's box is in the picture's px, so scale it with the picture. A sprite element's frame i = states.index(state) at ((i % cols) * frame.w, (i // cols) * frame.h); its rest state is the base picture (draw nothing over it)
rack-speaker.baked_words: the unit's legends are baked in (SPEAKER / CAPTURE and its buttons' engravings): see the handoff, section E

nixie-tubes.how: one tube a sheet, one row: frame i = states.index(digit) at (i * frame.w, 0). The frames are the lit glow only, made to lie over the Counter's face (rack-counter.webp, whose window holds the four unlit tubes): crop face_window_px from the face as the background (its tubes unlit, numerals showing), then draw each tube's frame at its tube_boxes_px (the face's px; the boxes overlap the window's top, where the frames are transparent). Alone on another background the frames show fringes. The face's other legends (COUNTER, ADDED DELAY ...) are the bench's: crop them out

namdev.how: the bench's stage NAM capture player in three wears (clean, played, beat). Element sprites namdev-<wear>-<id>.webp: one row; frame i = states.index(state) - 1 (frame 0 is the state after the rest)
